newsitem.title: INDIA: India to establish telecoms regulator.
newsitem.headline: India to establish telecoms regulator.

text.p: Indian President Shankar Dayal Sharma has issued an ordinance to create a regulatory authority for the telecommunications sector, a Communications Ministry statement said on Monday.

The statement said the independent Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) would provide a level playing field for fair competition and create further confidence in Indian and foreign investors in this sector.
A presidential ordinance is a temporary law which lapses if not subsequently approved by parliament. It was not clear when Sharma issued the decree.

The guidelines on private participation in basic telecom services, part of the National Telecom Policy, 1994, had proposed the setting up of the authority to resolve disputes between service providers, regulate tariffs and protect consumers interests.
